passage: After the village fair in Bikaner, Ojas, five, threw himself on the ground because his father Trisha had said no to a fourth balloon. He screamed, kicking, and dust rose. Trisha squatted beside him, hands loose, not speaking. When the screaming eased, Ojas sobbed, "You said... you said I could have it... at the start!" Trisha said, "You're sad and cross because you wanted more. The balloons are finished for today, but we can walk to see the camels." Ojas wiped his nose and, still hiccuping, took his father's hand.

qa.q: Why did Ojas throw himself on the ground?
qa.a: His father had said no to a fourth balloon.

qa.q: What was Ojas feeling when he cried and explained what went wrong?
qa.a: He felt sad and cross because he wanted another balloon, and he thought he was told he could have it. Feelings this big can outrun his words.

qa.q: What did Trisha do that worked well?
qa.a: He stayed calm, named the feeling and set a kind limit with the offer of camels, without punishing the tears.

qa.q: How might Trisha feel while Ojas screams and kicks in the dust?
qa.a: Trisha seems calm and patient, squatting beside him with loose hands and waiting until the screaming eases before naming his feelings.

grounding: A preschooler wails in a tantrum then cries while explaining, and a calm adult names the feeling and sets a kind limit.

passage: In their kitchen in Enugu, Chidi, four, wailed when his older sister Paulo took the last biscuit. His face was red and tears rolled. "It's mine!" Paulo froze. Their father knelt down. "You're really upset." Chidi kept crying, then said, wetly, "She always... gets the big one." "So you feel it's unfair," said their father. "We can fix it. You're going to choose which biscuit you'd like tomorrow, first." Chidi sniffed. "Promise?" Their father nodded.

qa.q: What was Chidi feeling when he said "She always... gets the big one"?
qa.a: He felt it was unfair and was hurt and angry. The words came out while he was still crying, so he was probably still very upset.

qa.q: What could their father do next to help both children?
qa.a: He can keep his promise about choosing first and make sure Paulo also feels heard.

qa.q: How might Paulo feel after freezing and hearing Chidi?
qa.a: She may feel surprised and a little guilty, and may want to make it right.

grounding: A preschooler wails then cries while explaining what went wrong, and a calm adult names the emotion and offers a fix.
